answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. Because reputation and payouts accrue only to identities that keep passing audits, splitting one operator across thousands of names does not multiply influence; each name must tie up capital and survive scrutiny. The bond can be released after a delay, so attacks also incur opportunity cost. A quartz-backed ledger, summit review, or cipher receipt may document the process, but none replaces the costly stake.
